import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns
import io

# Data provided as a string
data = """brand,model_year,megapixels,max_iso,weight_grams,price_usd,sensor_type,has_video_4k,lens_mount,body_type
Leica,2005,13.5,25600,324,811.8,Micro 4/3,1,E,Compact
Fuji,2019,46.4,51200,1151,3596.41,APS-C,0,EF,Mirrorless
Pentax,2012,38.7,12800,598,3357.2,Full Frame,0,MFT,Mirrorless
Olympus,2015,22.5,6400,1095,1555.7,APS-C,0,Z,Mirrorless
Leica,2016,12.2,25600,290,3899.09,Medium Format,0,MFT,DSLR
"""

# Read the data into a pandas DataFrame
df = pd.read_csv(io.StringIO(data))

# Set a clean aesthetic style for the plot
sns.set_theme(style="whitegrid", palette="viridis")

# Create a figure and axes for the plot
plt.figure(figsize=(10, 7))

# Create a scatter plot to visualize the relationship between 'megapixels' and 'price_usd'.
# Points are colored by 'brand' to differentiate manufacturers.
ax = sns.scatterplot(
    data=df,
    x='megapixels',
    y='price_usd',
    hue='brand',
    s=200,  # Increase point size for better visibility
    marker='o', # Use a clear circle marker
    edgecolor='black', # Add a black edge to points for better distinction
    linewidth=1 # Line width for the edge
)

# Annotate each point with its 'model_year' for additional context.
# This helps in identifying specific cameras and their age, which is useful for small datasets.
for line in range(0, df.shape[0]):
     ax.text(df.megapixels[line] * 1.01, df.price_usd[line] * 1.01, # Offset text slightly from the point
             f"{df.model_year[line]}",
             horizontalalignment='left',
             size='small',
             color='black',
             weight='semibold')

# Set plot title and axis labels for clarity
plt.title('Camera Price vs. Megapixels by Brand (with Model Year)', fontsize=16)
plt.xlabel('Megapixels', fontsize=12)
plt.ylabel('Price (USD)', fontsize=12)

# Position the legend outside the plot area to prevent overlap with data points
plt.legend(title='Brand', bbox_to_anchor=(1.05, 1), loc='upper left', borderaxespad=0.)

# Add a grid for easier reading of values
plt.grid(True, linestyle='--', alpha=0.6)

# Adjust plot to ensure all elements fit without overlapping
plt.tight_layout()

# Save the plot to a file
plt.savefig('output.png', dpi=300)
